# Vivid Builder API: integration guide for frontend developers

This file is for a frontend or mobile developer wiring a UI to the Vivid app
builder. It describes every endpoint, the streaming protocol, what to render,
and the order things happen in. It is exact as of the backend on branch
feat/app-builder. The human-readable design notes are in docs/builder.md and
DECISIONS.md at the repo root.

Base URL: the backend origin plus /v1 (dev: http://localhost:8000/v1).
Auth: every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`; see
section 0 for how to get one. Errors come as
`{"error": {"code", "message", "request_id"}, "detail": "..."}` with the HTTP
status. Codes worth branching on: busy (409), rate_limited (429),
not_configured (503), sandbox_unavailable (503), snapshot_failed (503),
bad_asset (400), not_found (404).

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. Authentication (Decane sign-in, then Vivid tokens)

Identity is Decane's: "Continue with Google" and emailed codes are handled
by Decane Connect, so this backend never sees a password. The client signs
the user in with Decane, then exchanges Decane's access token for Vivid's
own token pair, and uses the Vivid access token on every /v1 request.

Step 1, Decane. In the browser use Decane Connect with the public app id
(NEXT_PUBLIC_DECANE_APP_ID / the app's Decane app id). It returns a Decane
access token plus the Google profile when Google was used. The Vivid web
app's existing code for this lives in vivid-frontend/lib/backend/decane.ts;
the mobile app does the same with the emailed-code flow. Decane has no SDK;
it is a small HTTP flow.

Step 2, exchange:
  POST /auth/decane {access_token, name?, email?, picture?}
  -> {access_token, refresh_token, token_type: "bearer", user: {id, email, name, avatar_url, profile_email, created_at}}
The profile fields are display-only and optional (the token itself carries
no email); pass what Decane gave you so the account gets a name.

Step 3, use and refresh:
  Authorization: Bearer <access_token> on every request.
  Access tokens last 30 minutes, refresh tokens 30 days.
  POST /auth/refresh {refresh_token} -> a new pair. On any 401, refresh
  once and retry the request; if the refresh fails, sign in again.
  GET /auth/me -> the user; PATCH /auth/me {name} renames.

Store the pair in the client's secure storage (the web app keeps it in
localStorage under "vivid_tokens"; mobile uses the platform keystore).
Never store a Decane token beyond the exchange.

Long streams: a build turn can run 25 minutes, longer than an access token
lives. The token is checked when the request starts, so a stream in flight
is not cut off by expiry; refresh before the next request.

Developers and scripts: a `vivid_` API key (Settings, Developer in the web
app, or POST /keys with a session) works in the same header on every
/v1 route, including the builder. A key is its own account: projects it
creates belong to the key, not to the person who made it.

Dev only: POST /auth/signup and POST /auth/login with email and password
exist behind ALLOW_PASSWORD_AUTH=true for tests; they are off in production.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. The mental model

A project is a chat thread plus a live app in a cloud sandbox. Every message
the user sends is one "turn". The backend answers a turn as a Server-Sent
Events stream in the AI SDK UI Message Stream (v1) format, so a client
built on Vercel's `useChat` can consume it with no adapter; a hand-written
client parses `data: <json>` lines.

Lifecycle of a project:

1. create it (mode = "plan")
2. plan turns: the first message is expanded into a brief, then the model
   asks questions (rendered as cards), the user answers in text, the model
   writes a spec; the user may edit the spec
3. POST /build flips mode to "build"
4. build turns: the model writes the app; the preview iframe shows it; every
   changing turn stores a snapshot (a version)
5. optional: link Supabase (data and auth), enable Paystack (payments),
   upload assets (logo, photos) at any point
6. publish: a background job builds and puts the app on a live URL

Timing to design for: a plan turn is 15 to 90 seconds; a first build with
generated images is 15 to 25 minutes on the current models; an edit turn is
1 to 3 minutes; a publish is 1 to 3 minutes. Show progress, not a spinner.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Projects

POST   /builder/projects            {name?: string, skip_plan?: boolean}   -> Project (201)
GET    /builder/projects                                                  -> Project[]
GET    /builder/projects/{id}                                             -> Project
PATCH  /builder/projects/{id}       {name?, spec_md?, fullstack?}          -> Project
DELETE /builder/projects/{id}                                             -> 204 (kills sandbox, deletes snapshots and files)

Project:
{
  id, name,
  mode: "plan" | "build",
  brief_md: string | null,        // written by the prompt builder from the first message
  spec_md: string | null,         // the agreed spec; editable in plan mode
  current_snapshot_id: string | null,
  backend_mode: "none" | "byo" | "cloud",
  supabase_project_ref: string | null,
  payments_provider: "none" | "paystack",
  fullstack: boolean,             // accounts + server-side data were asked for (plan sets it)
  published_url: string | null,
  created_at, updated_at
}

`skip_plan: true` creates the project in build mode (for developers who
know what they want). Non-technical users should always go through plan
mode.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. The chat turn (the core of the UI)

POST /builder/projects/{id}/chat
Body: {"text": string, "images"?: string[]}   // images: https or data URLs, max 4, plan mode only (reference screenshots)
Response: 200, Content-Type text/event-stream, header x-vercel-ai-ui-message-stream: v1

One turn per project at a time: a second POST while one runs is 409 busy.
Cancel with POST /builder/projects/{id}/cancel -> {"cancelled": boolean}.
Rate limit: 429 rate_limited (10 turns a minute per user).

Reading the stream with fetch (SSE over POST, so EventSource cannot be used):

```ts
const res = await fetch(`${BASE}/builder/projects/${id}/chat`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
  body: JSON.stringify({ text }),
});
const reader = res.body!.getReader();
const decoder = new TextDecoder();
let buf = "";
for (;;) {
  const { value, done } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  buf += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });
  let i;
  while ((i = buf.indexOf("\n\n")) !== -1) {
    const frame = buf.slice(0, i); buf = buf.slice(i + 2);
    const line = frame.split("\n").find((l) => l.startsWith("data: "));
    if (!line) continue;
    const payload = line.slice(6);
    if (payload === "[DONE]") return;
    handle(JSON.parse(payload));
  }
}
```

With the AI SDK instead: `useChat({ transport: new DefaultChatTransport({ api: <url>, headers }) })`
where the URL points at this route (or at a same-origin route that pipes it
through unchanged). The message parts below are exactly what `useChat`
produces in `message.parts`.

### Parts, in the order they arrive

Every part is `{"type": ..., ...}`. Render by type; ignore unknown types.

Text (the model talking to the user):
  {"type":"text-start","id":"txt_x"}
  {"type":"text-delta","id":"txt_x","delta":"..."}      append to the text with that id
  {"type":"text-end","id":"txt_x"}

Steps (a model call plus its tool calls):
  {"type":"start-step"}  {"type":"finish-step"}         count them for "step 7 of 40"

Tool calls (what the agent is doing; show as a compact activity row):
  {"type":"tool-input-available","toolCallId":"c1","toolName":"write_file","input":{...}}
  {"type":"tool-output-available","toolCallId":"c1","output":"Wrote src/App.tsx (2131 chars).\nTypecheck: clean."}
  {"type":"tool-output-error","toolCallId":"c1","errorText":"error: ..."}
  Tool names and the label to show:
    read_file            "Reading src/App.tsx"
    write_file           "Writing src/pages/Shop.tsx"
    edit_file            "Editing src/App.tsx"
    list_files           "Looking at the files"
    run_command          "Running: npm install zustand"
    get_dev_server_logs  "Checking the dev server"
    generate_image       "Making a picture: <input.name>"   (input.kind: photo | lifestyle | logo | illustration)
    apply_migration      "Updating the database: <input.name>"
    deploy_edge_function "Deploying <input.name>"
    set_secret           "Storing a secret: <input.key>"   (the value is never in the stream)
    ask_user             plan mode: render input.questions as cards (see section 4)
    write_spec           plan mode: input.markdown is the spec

Data parts (custom events):
  {"type":"data-brief","data":{"markdown":"..."}}                 plan mode, first message: the expanded brief; show as a card the user can read
  {"type":"data-spec","data":{"markdown":"..."}}                  plan mode: the spec was written; offer "Edit spec" and "Build"
  {"type":"data-status","data":{"text":"Writing the app"}}       one plain sentence per phase: "Reading the project", "Writing the app", "Making pictures", "Checking the app against the spec", "Looking at the page on desktop and phone". Show the latest one as the progress line.
  {"type":"data-notice","data":{"text":"Retrying with a different model.","reason":"step_limit"|"typecheck_strikes"|"stream_retry","attempt"?:n}}
  {"type":"data-review","data":{"kind":"completeness","round":1}}   first builds: "Checking the app against the spec"
  {"type":"data-critique","data":{"round":1,"broken":false,"screenshots":[{"name":"desktop","width":1280,"url":"..."},{"name":"mobile","width":390,"url":"..."}]}}
        "Looking at the page on desktop and phone"; the URLs are time-limited (7 days) and safe to show as thumbnails. broken=true means the page crashed and the model is fixing it first.
  {"type":"data-usage","data":{"model":"...","steps":12,"tokens_in":..,"tokens_out":..,"reason":"answered"|"step_limit"|"typecheck_strikes"|"cancelled"|"error","mode"?:"plan"}}
  {"type":"data-snapshot","data":{"id":"...","seq":3}}            after finish: a new version exists; refresh the versions list

Control:
  {"type":"start","messageId":"msg_..."}   first part
  {"type":"finish"}                        last part before [DONE]
  {"type":"error","errorText":"..."}       the turn failed; the stream still ends with finish and [DONE]
  {"type":"abort","reason":"cancelled by the user"}

The assistant message is stored before `[DONE]` is sent, so fetching
messages right after the stream ends is safe.

### What to show during a build turn

- The preview iframe (section 6) updates live as files are written; keep it
  visible. Hot reload does the refreshing.
- An activity list from tool parts, newest at the bottom, collapsed by
  default for non-technical users, expanded for developers.
- The model's text parts as the assistant's chat bubbles.
- A progress line from start-step counts: "Step 12 of 40", then "Checking
  against the spec" on data-review, then "Looking at the page" on
  data-critique, then done on finish.
- data-notice as a small inline note, not a modal.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Plan mode

The first message of a new project produces, in one stream:
1. text parts: the brief, streamed as markdown (also in data-brief)
2. a tool-ask_user part with the questions
3. finish

Questions shape (tool-input-available, toolName "ask_user"):
```json
{"questions":[{"id":"audience","question":"Who is it for?","options":["Customers","Staff","Both"],"allow_free_text":true}]}
```
Render each as a card with tappable options and a free-text box when
allow_free_text. The user's choices are sent as the NEXT chat message in
plain text; one good format the model handles well:
  "Who is it for? -> Customers\nDo people sign in? -> Yes, with email"
There may be a second round of questions (at most two); then a write_spec
tool part arrives with the markdown spec and a data-spec part. The project
now has spec_md. Offer:
  - "Edit the spec": PATCH /builder/projects/{id} {spec_md}
  - "Build": POST /builder/projects/{id}/build -> Project (mode "build")
The user can also keep chatting in plan mode to change the spec.

Full-stack is opt-in. By default a project is a site (pages, catalogue,
forms, cart, an owner area behind a PIN, all in the browser). When the
user asks for accounts, sign-in, per-user records or says "full-stack",
the plan sets `fullstack: true` on the project and the spec's
Integrations says "Supabase (accounts, data)". Show a "Full-stack app"
toggle in project settings bound to PATCH {fullstack}. A full-stack
project needs a Supabase connection (section 8) before the build makes
accounts and data real; until then the build keeps local state and the
assistant's reply asks the user to connect Supabase. With both, the
builder follows its app-logic skill: profiles with roles, policies per
table, orders and bookings as state machines, edge functions for secrets.

Also in plan mode: uploads (section 7) are listed to the model and image
uploads are shown to it as pictures, so a user who uploads a logo and
product photos before answering gets a spec that names them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Messages (thread hydration)

GET /builder/projects/{id}/messages -> Message[]
Message: {id, role: "user"|"assistant", parts: Part[], model: string|null, created_at}

`parts` is the folded form of the stream: text deltas are one
{"type":"text","text"} part; a tool call is one
{"type":"tool-<name>","toolCallId","state":"output-available"|"output-error","input","output"|"errorText"};
step-start and data-* parts are kept in order; errors and aborts become
{"type":"data-error"|"data-abort","data":{...}}. A user message is
[{"type":"text","text"}, {"type":"file","mediaType":"image/*","url"}...].
This is the same shape `useChat` holds after a live stream, so reload the
thread from here into the same renderer.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Preview and files

GET /builder/projects/{id}/preview -> {url, sandbox_id, driver}
Put `url` in an iframe. The first call after idle starts a sandbox (5 to 10
seconds, up to 60 with a snapshot restore); show "Starting your workspace".
Call it again on a 503 sandbox_unavailable. Each call also keeps the sandbox
alive; sandboxes die after 10 idle minutes and come back from the latest
snapshot, so a stale iframe should be reloaded from a fresh preview call.

GET /builder/projects/{id}/files              -> {files: string[]}
GET /builder/projects/{id}/files/{path}       -> {path, content}
For a read-only code viewer (developers). Paths are project-relative.

### Runtime errors from the preview, and "Fix this"

The preview iframe is on another origin, so the client cannot read its
console. The app template relays errors instead: every uncaught error and
unhandled promise rejection in the preview is posted to the parent window:

  window.addEventListener("message", (e) => {
    if (e.data?.type === "vivid:error") show(e.data.message, e.data.stack);
  });

Show them in a small panel with a "Fix this" button that sends a chat turn:
"Fix this runtime error: <message>\n<first lines of stack>". The dev
server's own output (compile errors, Vite overlay text) is at
GET /builder/projects/{id}/logs?lines=100 -> {lines: string[]}; show it the
same way when the preview is blank.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. Uploads (logo, product photos, fonts)

POST   /builder/projects/{id}/assets   multipart field `file`   -> Asset (201)
GET    /builder/projects/{id}/assets                            -> Asset[]
DELETE /builder/projects/{id}/assets/{asset_id}                 -> 204
Asset: {id, name, mime, size_bytes, path: "/uploads/<name>", url: <time-limited>, meta: {width,height}|null, created_at}

Types: PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, SVG, AVIF, WOFF/WOFF2/TTF/OTF, PDF, MP4, MP3;
8 MB per file, 48 MB per project. Names are made URL-safe; re-uploading a
name replaces it. The app serves the file at `path`. Generated images the
model makes also appear here (that is how a client shows "pictures in this
project"). Show an upload control next to the chat; in plan mode the model
asks about pictures and the user uploads before answering.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 8. Versions

GET  /builder/projects/{id}/snapshots                 -> Snapshot[]  {id, seq, commit_sha, summary, size_bytes, created_at}
POST /builder/projects/{id}/snapshots                 -> Snapshot    (take one now; rarely needed)
POST /builder/projects/{id}/snapshots/{seq}/restore   -> Snapshot    (409 busy if a turn runs)
POST /builder/projects/{id}/undo                      -> Snapshot    one click back to the previous version (409 nothing_to_undo at version 1)

Every changing turn adds a version (data-snapshot on the stream). Restore
makes an older version current: a live sandbox gets the files at once, so
reload the preview iframe after it; the next turn's version continues the
sequence, nothing is lost. `summary` is the assistant's text for that turn,
good as the version label.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 9. Connectors: Supabase (data and auth) and Paystack (payments)

Connectors belong to the user, not the project; one connection serves all
their projects.

GET  /connectors                        -> [{id, provider, name, mode, projects?: [{ref, name, region, status}], created_at}]
POST /connectors {provider, token, public_key?}   -> connector (201) or 422 with a message to show
DELETE /connectors/{id}

Supabase, two ways:
  a) Button: GET /connectors/supabase/authorize -> {url}; open it (window.location or a popup).
     The backend's callback stores the connection and shows a "connected" page
     (or redirects to SUPABASE_OAUTH_RETURN_URL?connected=supabase if configured).
     503 not_configured means the OAuth app is not set up; fall back to (b).
  b) Paste: POST /connectors {provider:"supabase", token:"sbp_..."} (a personal access token).
Then per project:
  POST   /builder/projects/{id}/supabase {project_ref}            -> Project (backend_mode "byo")
         pick project_ref from the connector's `projects` list
  POST   /builder/projects/{id}/supabase {project_ref, url?, anon_key}   keys pasted, no connector (app env only, no tools)
  DELETE /builder/projects/{id}/supabase
From then on the model has migration, edge-function and secret tools, and the
app has VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY.

Paystack:
  POST /connectors {provider:"paystack", token:"sk_test_...", public_key:"pk_test_..."}
       both keys test or both live; the secret is verified and stored encrypted
  POST   /builder/projects/{id}/payments   -> Project (payments_provider "paystack")
  DELETE /builder/projects/{id}/payments
With a Supabase backend the model builds a verified checkout (orders table,
inline checkout, signed webhook). Tell the user, from the model's final
message, to add the webhook URL in their Paystack dashboard. Without a
backend the checkout is inline-only.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 10. Publish

POST /builder/projects/{id}/publish                -> Publish (202) {id, snapshot_id, url, status: "pending", error, created_at, updated_at}
GET  /builder/projects/{id}/publishes              -> Publish[] newest first
GET  /builder/projects/{id}/publishes/{publish_id} -> Publish

Poll the row every 3 to 5 seconds until status is "live" (url set; the
project's published_url updates too) or "failed" (error holds the build
log tail; show it, offer "Ask Vivid to fix it", which is just a chat turn
with that text). 409 busy while a turn or another publish runs. URLs look
like https://<name>-<id6>.vivid-apps.pages.dev until a custom domain exists.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 11. Usage

GET /builder/projects/{id}/usage -> {since, model_calls, tokens, sandbox_seconds, storage_bytes, cost_usd, by_kind}
Per-project totals for a usage panel. Per-user monthly rollups and plan
limits arrive with phase 6.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 12. Recommended screens

Non-technical flow: one input ("What do you want to build?"), the brief
card, question cards, "Edit spec / Build", then a two-pane view: chat left,
preview iframe right with a phone/desktop toggle (the iframe is the app; set
width 390 for phone), a small "Versions" list, an "Upload files" button, a
"Publish" button with the live link, and "Connect Supabase" / "Connect
Paystack" in project settings. Show tool activity collapsed.

Developer flow adds: skip plan on create, the file viewer, the spec as an
editable text area, the raw activity log, the usage panel.

Never show: vendor names from errors (the backend scrubs them), secret
values (never sent), the sandbox id.
